Also A + C < 180 = nθ so kθ < nθ, k ≤ n−1; and kθ > A ≥ 0 so k ≥ 1. Good.

Set x = kθ − A, with 0 < x < C, legal cut from C with P on AB. Children: T1 = (A, x, 180 − A − x) — the third angle is 180 − A − x = 180 − kθ = (n−k)θ, a positive integral multiple (since 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1, n−k ≥ 1). T2 = (B, C−x, A+x) — A + x = kθ, integral multiple. So both children carry a positive integral multiple of θ. Then regardless of Shan-Yu's discard, Lemma 1 finishes. This covers every initial triangle and every discard choice.

Children: T1 = (A, x, 180 − A − x) = (A, x, 180 − A − (θ − A)) = (A, x, 2θ − θ) = (A, x, θ). Yes, third angle is θ. T2 = (B, C − x, A + x) = (B, C − x, θ). Yes. Both children have an angle θ = 90°. Correct. So after one cut, Mulan wins regardless.

4. 180−A−x and A+x multiples ⇒ sum = 180 multiple — contradiction with (3). ✓.

Note: "positive integral multiple" — in case 4, sum is 180 which would be a positive multiple nθ; contradicts 180/θ ∉ ℤ. In cases 1–3, differences/sums of positive multiples are positive multiples. Good.
